name: Local LLM Layer
description: Foundations of the local-model layer (19s-1): an async request queue with a per-year budget and a situation cache over the advisor endpoint, fixed-schema grounding digests, and a yearly in-character Chronicle of your empire on the Galactic History screen (a plain digest when no model answers); optionally (19s-3) a yearly model-chosen strategic move among the legal moves of the AI empires nearest you, applied as recorded commands; optional Voices (19s-2) give messages, decisions and council speeches in-character text. The model never runs inside the tick; its only effect on the game is the optional strategic moves, each a recorded command, and the optional in-character text. Includes the Event Log scenario (and with it Internal Security and the Emergent Galaxy packages; their own flags).

flags.name: llmFoundations
flags.label: Local model layer
flags.description: Queue, digests and the yearly Chronicle (needs the advisor endpoint in Settings; without a model the Chronicle is the plain digest).

flags.name: llmStrategic
flags.label: Model-driven strategy for nearby empires
flags.description: Once a year each of the AI empires nearest you makes one deliberate move chosen by the local model among its legal moves (council motions and votes, peace terms, war goals, investigations, concessions, league offers, the herder path). Needs the local model layer; every choice is checked and applied as a recorded command, and the game's own rules keep running.

flags.name: llmArchivist
flags.label: Archivist + spoken orders
flags.description: Needs the local model layer. An Ask tab on Galactic History answers questions from what your empire knows (the event log, the chronicle, the digest; plain matching records when no model answers), and an Orders tab turns a typed order into one legal command, issued only after you confirm it.

flags.name: llmVoices
flags.label: Voices
flags.description: In-character text for existing messages and decisions (spymaster, chancellor and marshal briefings, faction ultimatums, council speeches, the Concord greeting, herder lore, scheme letters) and a diplomat grounded on the reputation ledger and claims. Needs the local model layer; without a model the scripted text stays.
